claims.statement: Carrier Operations implies knowledge of a lag on the affected feed and requires slot corrections before replay allocations can run safely.
claims.corroboration: Carrier Ops statement uses language 'affected feed and its lag' and prescribes slot correction before allocation replay, suggesting they have identified a lag condition.
claims.limitation: Carrier Ops does not explicitly state what the lag is, where it originates (dock congestion, carrier capacity, feed processing delay), or whether it's specific to split-reservation format orders. Requires dock capacity check to isolate the blockage point.

claims.statement: East-node carrier feed experiences a lag or blockage preventing pickup of EXC-0921 orders; this lag appears correlated with v18 deployment but may be independent infrastructure issue.
claims.corroboration: Timing (v18 at 22:00, lag apparent at 06:00), geography (east-node only), and Carrier Ops language all point to feed lag. Inventory control and dock schedule visual check found nothing obvious, but observability gap (m8_e09) means we cannot yet see carrier-side confirmation.
claims.limitation: Lag exists but root cause unknown: is it (a) v18 split-reservation format incompatible with carrier protocol, triggering their lag, (b) east-node dock is saturated, or (c) independent carrier feed issue coincidentally timed with v18? Dock capacity check will discriminate.

claims.statement: Root cause is carrier-feed lag on east-node lanes preventing pickup of v18-allocated split-reservation orders, trigger unknown.
claims.corroboration: All evidence converges on lag: Carrier Ops prescribes slot corrections, observability alert is geographic (east-node only), inventory counts reconcile, and Inventory Control audit shows 100% of EXC-0921 orders are held.
claims.limitation: Lag is confirmed but root cause within the lag is not. Is it dock congestion, carrier capacity, or split-reservation incompatibility? Dock capacity check needed to determine whether to revert v18 or apply slot corrections.

contradictions.claim_a: Regression suite was green and change review passed for v18.
contradictions.claim_b: v18 deployment correlates with carrier feed lag on east-node lanes.
contradictions.description: Regression suite may not have tested carrier-feed lag scenarios or may have used test data that did not expose the pattern. Or the lag is truly independent and timing is coincidental.
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: Dock capacity check will discriminate: if dock is saturated, lag may be independent of v18; if dock is normal, split-reservation format or east-node allocation pattern from v18 likely triggered lag.

capability_gaps.capability: East-node dock capacity, queue depth, and congestion status during 06:00-current window.
capability_gaps.reason: Discriminates whether lag is dock-saturation (independent of v18) or carrier-integration (v18-triggered). If dock is normal, split-reservation format likely caused carrier rejection; if dock is saturated, may be unrelated infrastructure issue.

capability_gaps.capability: Carrier-side confirmation: do they see and accept split-reservation format, or do they reject it?
capability_gaps.reason: Would discriminate C6 (format incompatibility) from C9 (feed lag). Currently uncertain whether carriers cannot see orders, cannot process format, or simply have logistical lag.

next_action.rationale: Verify east-node dock capacity, queue depth, and congestion during the 06:00-current window. If dock is at capacity or backed up, lag is likely infrastructure-limited and independent of v18; if dock is normal, v18's split-reservation pattern likely triggered carrier feed lag. This discriminates root cause: revert v18 (if carrier format incompatibility) vs. apply slot corrections (if dock saturation)
next_action.expected_information_gain: High. Dock capacity check isolates the root cause mechanism within the confirmed carrier-feed lag, enabling decision between revert_allocation_ruleset and apply_slot_correction mitigations.
